text:
aditya: FYI - us-west2 GNode-47 saw NVMe IOPS collapse during an autoscale event. GPU attach waits jumped and some jobs timed out.
marie: Which device & what metrics?
aditya: nvme1n1. Snapshot: iostat shows huge write queue and svc time.
```
iostat -x 1 2
Device:       rrqm/s wrqm/s r/s    w/s  rsec/s  wsec/s avgrq-sz avgqu-sz await  svctm  %util
nvme1n1        0.00  0.00  0.00  450.0  0.00  22500.0 50.00     9.8    95.2  1.40   99.9
```
aditya: avgqu-sz ~9.8 and await ~95ms. SMART shows temp 78C and media_errors incremented.
oliver: Did janitor start a deep scrub or full fstrim? I remember a scheduled run in that rack.
aditya: Janitor logs: "start_scan nvme1n1 mode=full shards=4" at 7161239800. Also see kernel blk settings changed 7161239700 (requeue_depth=128).
jen: We rolled requeue_depth bump in the last kernel build to improve throughput for small-block workloads. Looks like for certain NVMe firmware this increases queue depth too aggressively and saturates device under mixed IO.
marie: Interesting. So combined effect: janitor full-scan (heavy sequential writes) + higher queue_depth => device saturation => GPU_attach waits.
srebot: scrub-throttle-controller: policy was set to default concurrency=4. No backpressure hook for gpu_provision backlog.
oliver: Short term ops: 1) pause janitor on gnode-47, 2) set node to DRAIN for new GPU allocs, 3) failover pending attaches to us-west2-fallback pool.
aditya: Pausing janitor: `curl -XPOST https://infra-api.internal/janitor/gnode-47/actions -d '{"action":"pause"}'` returning 202. Kicking drain: `infractl node drain gnode-47 --reason "nvme-high-await"`.
jen: Cost note: moving jobs to fallback pool will bump egress + preemption costs; estimated $1200/day if sustained. We should balance speed of mitigation vs cost.
marie: Medium-term: janitor should consult node health (temp/media_errors/util) before starting full-scan. Also caps on concurrent shards based on gpu_provision_backlog metric.
aditya: Agree. I'll open INF-4007 with logs & iostat; proposed immediate mitigations: revert requeue_depth change on canary (20% hosts), and add a janitor guard (skip full when temp>72C or media_errors>0).
oliver: Also recommend an alert: alert when avgqu-sz>5 and gpu_provision_backlog>3 for >2m. Page infra-pager if seen.
srebot: deploy-bot: rollback PR #901 queued at 7161239900. Canary rollout started.
aditya: After pausing janitor and rollback canary, avg await dropped to ~18ms in 3m and GPU attach latency normalized.
oliver: (typo) oliver: Nice.
jen: Schedule hardware replacement for nvme1n1 once node drained; mark as high-rotation priority.
aditya: I'll add the SMART time-series to INF-4007 and include the cost impact table.
marie: Postmortem items: root cause analysis, safety gates for janitor & kernel param tuning, alert & runbook update, capacity contingency playbook. Assign owners.
oliver: I'll take the runbook update.
aditya: Taking janitor guard patch & PR.
jen: I'll own the cost impact and fallback pool sizing for us-west2.
marie: If rollback doesn't hold on canary or we see recurrence in 30m, page infra-pager.
aditya: Closing for now; will update INF-4007 when PRs are up.
